system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The LLM is then queried with a prompt that includes the initial state, the low-level executable action space, the replay buffer of random actions, and a description of the domain in natural language
system_prompt_style.note: Per-game prompt files under abstraction_prompts/ (file tree); rendering code not in bundle. Not a tool-using system prompt.

env_context_strategy.note: Game state injected as text in prompt; no repository context applicable; category does not fit a game world-model synthesizer.

context_compaction.note: config.py has max_revision_transitions/max_revision_tokens and revision_mode, suggesting replay-buffer limiting, but the code applying it is not in the bundle.

observation_format.evidence_quote: We use games suitable to test LLM-style agents that have text-based state representations

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: The prompt asks the LLM to generate an initial Python low-level transition function.
tool_call_format.note: Closest value: the LLM emits Python world-model code and PDDL, not actions; actions come from Fast Downward + BFS planner. No tool-calling interface.

tool_count.evidence_quote: Note that TheoryCoder differs in that the LLM is only used to refine the python world model given state transitions, and does not directly revise plans given feedback.
tool_count.note: No tools exposed to the model; LLM only synthesizes code.

edit_primitive.note: LLM regenerates the transition model; output merging code not in bundle.

protocol_standardization.note: No dependency files or full source in bundle to grep.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: If the high-level plan is not successfully achieved, the world model undergoes refinement, either by correcting explicit errors or identifying discrepancies through exploratory goals.
loop_primitives.note: Plan (Fast Downward) -> BFS -> execute -> compare predicted vs actual -> LLM refine.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Fast-Downward outputs a high-level plan in terms of the operators that were used in the PDDL domain file.
planning_granularity.note: PDDL plan produced by a classical planner, not the LLM.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: TheoryCoder uses GPT-4o (OpenAI, 2024a) to generate and refine programs.

delegation_mechanism.note: Runner modes show no delegation; full agent code not in bundle.

short_term_state.note: Fields include plan_str, operators, predicates, worldmodel, exploratory_plans.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: with in-YAML `transfer:` blocks so downstream levels inherit the learned world model from earlier ones.
long_term_memory.note: Learned PDDL/worldmodel.py files transferred across levels; closest value.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: All wrappers are **resume-safe**: they skip cells whose logs show a win marker, so you can Ctrl-C and re-invoke.
state_persistence.note: Skip completed cells, not resume of a run; DomainMode.EXISTING reuses existing artifacts.

self_verification.evidence_quote: It compares the predicted transitions and actual transitions to see if there are any mismatches.
self_verification.note: Closest value: harness executes plan in environment and feeds prediction errors back.

retry_policy.note: max_revisions=5; paper: up to 5 retries per level.

termination_condition.note: Level ends on win; attempts capped by max_attempts=6.

cost_controls.note: max_revision_tokens=30000 caps revision prompt, not spend.

timeouts.note: Planner timeout, default None; paper gives planner 500s.

execution_isolation.note: Fast Downward run as host subprocess; LLM-generated worldmodel.py imported via sys.path in-process.

tracing.evidence_quote: Each cell contains the learned PDDL domain, problem file, Python world model, plans, timings, and a summary of win/loss.

target_domain.evidence_quote: learning transferable world models by jointly synthesising PDDL abstractions and Python transition functions with an LLM.
target_domain.note: Grid-world games (VGDL, BabyAI, MiniHack, Baba is You).

primary_artifact.note: Repo at main is TheoryCoder-2, diverging from TMLR 2025 paper (GPT-4o, temp 0.7 vs config 1.0).

first_release_date.note: No tag/commit dates; paper v2 dated 13 Jul 2025, v1 date not given.

pinned_version.note: No tagged release; full hash not given.
